# Validation

- An `AsyncRule` passes `passes()` unconditionally. `fails()`, `passes()`, `validate()` and `FormValidator.rules` never run it; only `Validator.validateAsync()` does. A uniqueness or existence rule therefore accepts bad input on any sync path.
- Give a custom rule a `message()` that is a translation key (`validation.<name>`). `Rule.name`, the key of `FormValidator`'s `messages` overrides, is derived from it, because `runtimeType.toString()` is minified in release builds and an override keyed on it would stop matching in production. A rule whose message is a raw sentence overrides `name`.
- A rule that compares size (`Min`, `Max`, `Between`) extends `SizeRule` and implements `passesSized`. A string is sized by value only when the same field also carries `Numeric` or `Integer`, and by length otherwise. A rule cannot see its siblings, so every runner has to pass `SizeRule.numericIn(rules)` as `numeric:`, as `Validator` and `FormValidator` do.
